name: How to Build and Waterproof a Recessed Shower Niche Properly

step.name: Step 1: Choose location and confirm stud framing
step.text: Select an interior shower wall away from the main shower head spray. Verify that no supply pipes, vent stacks, or electrical cables run through the selected stud bay.

step.name: Step 2: Install horizontal structural blocking
step.text: Cut and fasten horizontal 2x4 framing members between studs at your desired rough opening height. Ensure blocking is level, plumb, and secured with structural screws to support the niche box.

step.name: Step 3: Secure the niche unit flush with wall backer
step.text: Mount your prefabricated waterproof niche box or approved backer board assembly into the opening. Make sure the outer flange sits flush with the adjacent wall backer panels to avoid uneven tile lips.

step.name: Step 4: Seal all perimeter joints and fastener points
step.text: Apply manufacturer-approved waterproof sealant and embedding fabric bands over the entire seam where the niche meets the wall. Fully coat all fastener penetrations to maintain a continuous, unbreached barrier.

step.name: Step 5: Slope the bottom sill toward the shower
step.text: Check that the bottom shelf slopes slightly forward—roughly one-sixteenth to one-eighth inch—so standing water drains off the sill directly into the shower pan rather than collecting against the back corner.

step.name: Step 6: Tile, trim, and seal the finished niche
step.text: Set tile using high mortar coverage, install clean edge profiles along outer corners, and seal all interior plane transitions with flexible silicone sealant instead of brittle grout. What to Expect During the Process Modifying framing and tying into waterproofing systems requires precision.
